command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Errors.Invalid..why: A shared low-level validation check failed somewhere in the request — a required field was left empty, malformed, or out of range. The exact wording is reused verbatim by dozens of unrelated checks across the command layer (most often identity-provider configuration fields, domain names, and settings values), so the field at fault depends on the specific error ID's call site, not the message text.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|ID missing.why: A required ID field on the request was left empty. The check is shared across dozens of unrelated resource types (schemas, SMTP/SMS configs, actions, applications, and more), so which ID is missing depends on the specific call site, not the message text.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Resource Owner.why: The request omitted the organization ID (resourceOwner) that the target resource belongs to — every one of these commands needs an org ID to know which event stream to operate on.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|User ID missing.why: The target user's ID was left empty on a user-scoped command such as deactivate, lock, reactivate, remove, or sign-out — ZITADEL needs a concrete user ID to know which account to act on.

command|NOT_FOUND|Identity Provider Conf.why: The instance-level identity provider (LDAP, SAML, generic OIDC, or a Zitadel provider) referenced by ID for an update or certificate-regeneration request doesn't exist — it was never created, or has already been removed.

command|NOT_FOUND|User could not be foun.why: The user ID passed to the command doesn't correspond to an existing user — it was never created, or the account has already been deleted.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|User could n.why: Phone commands (add, verify, resend a code, remove) resolve the owning user first — the user's write model shows the account doesn't exist or was already removed, leaving no user to attach the phone number to.

command|NOT_FOUND|Private Label Policy n.why: The organization hasn't configured a custom branding/label policy yet, so a request to change it or manage its logo/icon assets has no existing policy to act on.

command|INTERNAL|An internal error occur.why: Building or pushing the underlying event(s) for the request failed unexpectedly — e.g. an eventstore write failure — rather than anything being wrong with the request's contents. This points to a server-side/infra issue rather than a fixable input.

command|NOT_FOUND|Default Private Label.why: The instance-wide default branding/label policy hasn't been set up yet, so a request to change it or add a default logo/icon/font has nothing to operate on.

command|INTERNAL|Object not created.why: Uploading a label-policy asset (logo or icon) to the configured object storage backend failed, so the file was never persisted.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|No changes.why: The update request's values are identical to what's already stored, so there's nothing new to persist. This guard is shared by many 'change X' commands — OIDC/SAML app config, application name, OIDC settings — whenever the computed diff is empty.

command|NOT_FOUND|SMTP configuration not.why: The SMTP configuration referenced by its (resourceOwner, id) pair doesn't exist — wrong ID, wrong org, or it was already removed — so it can't be changed, activated, or deleted.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Multifactor.why: An OTP check (TOTP, or OTP via SMS/email) was attempted before the user finished setting up that factor — its state isn't 'ready' yet, so there's no verified secret to check the submitted code against.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Application inv.why: The application payload failed basic validation — a required field like the app name is empty, or a type-specific requirement for the OIDC/SAML/API configuration wasn't met.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Code is invalid.why: The submitted verification code — an init code, or a passwordless/passkey registration code — doesn't match what was generated and stored for this user, or it has expired.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Multifactor inv.why: The second-factor or multi-factor type passed when adding or removing a factor from a login policy isn't a recognized value — e.g. it was left unspecified.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Identity Pro.why: The identity provider ID referenced when starting a login/linking intent, or when adding an IDP link to a user, doesn't correspond to any IDP configured on the org or instance.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|User is lock.why: The user's account is currently locked — typically from too many failed verification attempts — so further recovery-code checks or removal are rejected until it's unlocked.

command|NOT_FOUND|Project not found.why: The project ID doesn't resolve to an existing project under the given organization — never created, wrong org, or already removed.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Metadata is inv.why: A metadata key in the request is empty or otherwise fails validation when setting or bulk-removing metadata on a user or organization.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|SAML Metadata f.why: The SAML metadata XML — supplied directly or fetched from the metadata URL — couldn't be parsed as valid SAML metadata for the identity provider.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|SAML metadata i.why: A metadata URL was given for a SAML identity provider, but fetching the XML from that URL failed, so no metadata was available to configure the provider despite the name.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Organisation.why: The organization ID referenced by the command — as the target org, the granted org on a user grant, or the org a group is being created in — doesn't exist.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|User ID miss.why: An internal session or MFA-setup helper needed the session's associated user ID, but it was empty — the session hasn't been linked to a user yet.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|User is not.why: The target user is still in the 'initial' state — they haven't completed their invite/first-login flow — so actions that assume an active account, like requesting a password reset or verifying an email, are rejected until then.

command|NOT_FOUND|Application doesn't ex.why: The application referenced by project ID + app ID doesn't exist — never created or already removed — so it can't be renamed, have its secret regenerated, or be deleted.

command|NOT_FOUND|Errors.NotFound.why: A referenced resource couldn't be located — depending on the call site, the object a permission check needed an owning org for, an organization-settings record, or an instance membership.

command|NOT_FOUND|SMS configuration not.why: The SMS provider configuration referenced by (resourceOwner, id) doesn't exist, or exists but isn't the provider type — Twilio vs. generic HTTP — the command expected.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Execution is in.why: An action-v2 execution condition must set exactly one of its mutually exclusive selectors (method/service/'all', or event/group/'all') — none, or more than one, was set.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Project member.why: The project ID, target user ID, or role list is missing, or one of the given roles isn't a valid project role, when adding, changing, or removing a project member.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Code not fou.why: A code check (email, phone, or OTP) was attempted before a code was ever requested for this user — no code is on record, or the configured code provider is missing.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Refresh Toke.why: During an OIDC token refresh, the presented refresh token doesn't match a currently active session, has passed its absolute or idle expiration, or doesn't parse into ZITADEL's expected <sessionID>:<tokenID> format.

command|NOT_FOUND|Code not found.why: There's no pending verification code for this user — verifying an email code, resending an init code, or sending a passwordless-init code was requested with no outstanding code on record.

command|NOT_FOUND|Execution condition is.why: An action-v2 execution's condition references an event name, event group, or function identifier that doesn't exist in ZITADEL's registry of executable conditions.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|ClientID missin.why: The Apple identity provider's Services ID (client ID) field was left empty when adding or updating an Apple IDP configuration.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Code is empty.why: A verification code (phone, email, or OTP) was submitted as an empty string when trying to verify it.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Errors.Project..why: The project ID, user ID, role list, or org/grant ID is missing when adding or changing a project grant member, or one of the given roles isn't a valid project-grant role.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Id missing.why: A user grant ID — or one of the IDs in a bulk-remove list — was left empty when deactivating or removing a grant.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Invalid Private.why: The private key bytes supplied for an Apple identity provider couldn't be parsed as a valid key — the content is malformed or corrupted.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|KeyID missing.why: The Apple identity provider's Key ID field, which identifies which private key signs the client secret, was left empty when adding or updating an Apple IDP configuration.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|Password is emp.why: A password value was left empty when setting, changing, or checking a user's password — or, for a hash-based set, neither a plaintext password nor an encoded hash was given.

command|INVALID_ARGUMENT|TeamID missing.why: The Apple identity provider's Developer Team ID field was left empty when adding or updating an Apple IDP configuration.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Code is empt.why: A resend-code request — phone or email, on either the schema-user or human-user model — was made, but no code has ever been generated for this user; there's nothing to resend until an initial code is created.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Errors.Org.D.why: Loading the org's domain/username policy (falling back to the instance default) failed while validating a username change or user removal — this wraps whatever underlying lookup error occurred, rather than pointing at one specific missing setting.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Errors.User..why: The user ID supplied — or auto-generated — when creating a human or machine user already belongs to an existing user account.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|ID missing.why: An internal WebAuthn/passkey helper — registering or verifying a credential, or sending a passwordless init code — needed the user ID, and sometimes a credential ID, but received an empty value.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Project Gran.why: The project grant's resource owner doesn't match the actual owning org of the project, or the grant is being created for the project's own organization — an org mismatch on the grant.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Project not.why: The project ID doesn't resolve to an active project for the given org. This is the same underlying condition as the NOT_FOUND variant, surfacing here because the project is checked as a precondition of another command rather than as its direct target.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Role is inva.why: A project role's resource owner doesn't match the resource owner of the project it's being added to or changed on — the role and its parent project disagree about which org owns them.

command|FAILED_PRECONDITION|Token is inv.why: An OIDC access token being checked against a session doesn't match the session's current token, the session isn't active, or the token has already expired.

command|NOT_FOUND|Action not found.why: The (deprecated v1) action ID referenced doesn't exist for the given organization — never created, or already removed.

command|NOT_FOUND|Device Authorization R.why: The device code presented when approving or canceling an OAuth device-authorization flow doesn't match any pending request — a wrong, expired, or already-completed device code.

command|NOT_FOUND|Errors.Instance.DebugN.why: The instance's debug notification provider — a test sink that logs or writes notifications to a file instead of sending them — hasn't been configured, so there's nothing to change or remove.

command|NOT_FOUND|Login Policy not found.why: The organization hasn't configured its own login policy, so a request to modify it — adding an IDP, removing the policy — has no existing policy to act on.

command|NOT_FOUND|Multifactor not existi.why: The second-factor or multi-factor method being removed from a login policy (instance-wide default or org-level) was never added, or has already been removed.

command|NOT_FOUND|Multifactor OTP (OneTi.why: The user never set up a TOTP or OTP-via-email second factor, or already removed it, so there's nothing to verify or delete.

command|NOT_FOUND|Organisation not found.why: The organization ID doesn't correspond to an existing org — never created, or already removed — when trying to rename, reactivate, or delete it.

command|NOT_FOUND|Phone not found.why: The target user has no phone number on file to verify, resend a code for, or remove. One v2 phone-event code path reuses this same message when the user account itself no longer exists, so it isn't always literally about the phone.

command|INTERNAL|unable to unmarshal app.why: An application lifecycle event (changed or deactivated) stored in the eventstore couldn't be deserialized back into its expected Go struct while replaying event history — a sign of corrupted event data or an incompatible struct change, not a bad request.

command|INTERNAL|unable to unmarshal lab.why: Despite the message text, this comes from the project-grant-member event mapper (changed/removed events), not label-policy code — the stored event payload couldn't be deserialized while replaying history from the eventstore.

command|INTERNAL|unable to unmarshal pro.why: A project-grant lifecycle event (removed, or cascade-changed) stored in the eventstore couldn't be deserialized back into its expected Go struct while replaying event history.
